summary:
Lunar Landing Site Evaluator is an interactive 3D astrodynamic and terrain-aware web application designed to address the extreme lighting and communication constraints of missions to the Moon’s south pole. While existing mission planning tools feature complex interfaces that hinder rapid evaluation, our dual-mode platform bridges engineering precision and public space literacy.
For mission planners, Mission Planner Mode integrates analytical Sun-Earth-Moon ephemeris models with 360° crater-ridge horizon masking (modeled on NASA LRO LOLA DEM concepts) to evaluate solar elevation angles, power generation potential, and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication windows. Users can compare curated landing sites (Apollo, CLPS, Artemis targets) or custom coordinates across lunar seasons, run 5 km micro-site optimizations, adjust solar mast heights, and assess Earth-to-Moon transfer Delta-V and DSN link budgets. For educators and the general public, Educator / Public Mode offers one-click guided space stories that demystify lunar libration, peaks of eternal light, and far-side relay requirements.
details:
The Lunar Landing Site Evaluator is a browser-based mission-planning and educational simulation suite built with Three.js (WebGL), Chart.js, and analytical astrodynamic equations. It visualizes real-time 3D Sun–Earth–Moon orbital mechanics alongside a site-specific Local Horizon Sky Dome and 360° Horizon Panorama. By overlaying 360° terrain-elevation masks onto solar and Earth-libration trajectories, the engine dynamically calculates sunlit duration, countdowns to sunset/Earthset, Direct-to-Earth (DTE) visibility windows, and real-time LOS BLOCKED BY TERRAIN alerts.

Key Features and Benefits

Dual-Mode Accessibility: Mission Planner Mode provides Go/No-Go viability scoring, 5-in-1 telemetry timelines, 13-month seasonal oscillations, 3σ landing-dispersion analysis, Earth-to-Moon transfer Delta-V budgets, and Deep Space Network (DSN) link margins. Educator/Public Mode features three interactive 60-second guided scenarios: Peak of Eternal Light, Earth’s Figure-8 Libration, and Lunar Far-Side Comms.

Active Site and Hardware Optimization: Includes a Solar Mast Height Simulator (1 m–15 m) to evaluate how elevating solar arrays clears low crater ridges, an Auto-Optimize Micro-Site tool (5 km scan) to pinpoint optimal coordinates, and a Global Candidate Matrix for side-by-side, multi-site, multi-date comparison.

Tools, Languages, and Software Used

Developed using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), Three.js for 3D WebGL rendering, and Chart.js for interactive engineering telemetry. Super Intelligence (AI) tools were used to assist with code debugging, UI layout optimization, and visual presentation structuring.

Creativity and Design Considerations

Rather than treating the Moon as a smooth sphere, we incorporated realistic ridge masking and hardware mitigation—such as mast height and micro-site shifting—to reflect real Artemis engineering trade-offs, while ensuring zero-installation browser accessibility and clear visual feedback for students and the general public.
